details: Bitcoin experienced a significant drop, falling below $68,000 to its lowest point since August. This downturn is attributed to a confluence of bearish factors, including a strengthening US Dollar, increased expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike following a hotter-than-expected October CPI report, and substantial net outflows from US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), totaling over $2.5 billion since October 30. Additionally, political uncertainties in the US, suggesting potential for stricter crypto regulation after the recent midterm elections, further weighed on investor sentiment.
title: Bitcoin Plummets Below $68K Amid Macroeconomic and ETF Pressures

details: The International Energy Agency (IEA) has reported that global oil supply surpassed demand in October, marking the first surplus since the commencement of the war in Iran. This development follows statements from US President Donald Trump indicating that the conflict with Iran was "effectively over," leading to Brent crude prices falling to their lowest levels since late August. Despite this, concerns persist regarding continued attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East and the possibility of further US military actions.
title: Global Oil Supply Returns to Surplus as Iran War Nears End
